comments.note: DapperTagsRepository.MergeTagAsync: No guard for sourceTagId == targetTagId. If called with identical IDs, Step 1 would INSERT IGNORE (no-op due to unique key) then DELETE all tags_movies rows for that tag — data destructive. The ViewModel likely prevents this scenario, but the repository has no explicit assertion. Low priority since the call site controls input.

DapperTagsRepository.GetMergeImpactAsync: If sourceTagId == targetTagId, the OverlapMovies INNER JOIN self-joins on the same tag and returns the count of all movies with that tag (rather than a true overlap count). Not a regression — the field didn't exist before — but worth noting if the UI ever needs to handle the same-tag edge case.

DapperTagsRepository.MergeTagAsync transaction pattern correctly mirrors DeleteTagAsync. The ambient-tx guard (catch InvalidOperationException on BeginTransaction) is consistent with the established pattern, confirming correctness under test-fixture rollback scenarios.

comments.note: No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified. A03 (Injection): GetMergeImpactAsync uses @SourceTagId and @TargetTagId in multi-line parameterized SQL; all 5 steps of MergeTagAsync use @SourceTagId/@TargetTagId with anonymous-object params — including INSERT IGNORE ... SELECT patterns. No string concatenation in any SQL. A04 (Insecure Design): sourceTagId==targetTagId edge case noted by QA is data-destructive but not a security concern; ViewModel prevents it at runtime. A09 (Logging): no audit logging for the merge operation — consistent with existing repository-layer pattern; informational only.
